title: Add a finalize_attempt tool the runner calls to close the artifact boundary
description:
Objective: let the runner, not the CLI's exit, declare that a task's bytes are final. An interactive TUI seat that stays open must still be able to finalize, and a provider mode without one-shot semantics needs an explicit operation instead of an implicit exit.

Deliverable: a new tool in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/finalizeAttempt.ts, registered in getTools() in tools/index.ts, which moves an attempt from finalizing to closed after the runner reports its landing outcome. It carries the attempt id and generation and is fenced by assertAttemptCurrent, so a late call from a superseded attempt is rejected. Closing releases the claim hold added by the finalizing sibling task.

Not in scope: the wrapper actually calling it, which is the sibling wrapper task; candidate and receipt records, which are separate. Registration in getTools() is mandatory — an unregistered tool is silently invisible to MCP.

Unskips the acceptance case "fast QA cannot finish before candidate preparation" in src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts, which must pass unchanged.

Verification: npx vitest run src/tools/finalizeAttempt.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.

Read src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from the describe at line 1008 through line 1172, and read its `captureRefusal` helper at line 138: it awaits the call, fails outright if the call RESOLVES, and requires an instance of MoeError. Note the four things it demands. First, `moe.claim_next_task` is called with `runnerId` and `workspace` alongside statuses/taskId/workerId, and returns flat `attemptId` and `generation`. Second, the finalizing refusal must be THROWN with numeric code -32002, codeName exactly `ATTEMPT_FINALIZING`, and a context carrying `attemptId` and `retryable: true`. Third, `moe.qa_approve` must refuse the same way while an attempt is finalizing, on the no-workerId human path. Fourth, `moe.finalize_attempt` takes taskId, workerId, runnerId, attemptId, generation, outcome and landedRevision, closes the attempt, and a byte-identical second call must leave the attempt file unchanged. Now confirm what actually shipped in the prerequisite: src/util/claimGuards.ts line 40 exports `CLAIM_ATTEMPT_FINALIZING`, and src/tools/claimNextTask.ts around line 185 RETURNS an object carrying that string as `code` rather than throwing, and nothing in src/tools/qaApprove.ts holds on a finalizing attempt at all. Both gaps trace to the plan for task-5dd49fe2, which chose a non-throwing shape from the retryable rail; the acceptance case expresses retryable as `context.retryable` on a thrown state conflict instead. Correcting both is therefore in scope here by necessity, not scope creep. Finally read `assertAttemptCurrent` in src/util/enforcement.ts line 148 and note the trap that decides the design: it resolves the current attempt through `currentAttempt`, which only ever returns a NON-closed attempt, so calling it on an already-closed attempt would refuse with ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED and break the required idempotency. Produce no diff in this step.

implementationPlan.description: WRITE THE FINALIZE TOOL. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/finalizeAttempt.ts following the shape of the neighbouring tool modules: an exported factory returning a ToolDefinition with name `moe.finalize_attempt`, an input schema declaring taskId, workerId, runnerId, attemptId, generation, outcome and landedRevision with `additionalProperties: false`, and a handler that runs its whole body inside `state.runExclusive`. Do NOT set `blocking: true` — a task rail forbids it, and this tool never parks. Handler order is the design, and the idempotency trap from step 1 dictates it. First validate the inputs and refuse malformed ones as invalid input. Then load the attempt by id and refuse a missing one, and one whose taskId does not match the supplied task, with named errors. Then handle the already-closed case BEFORE any fencing: when the attempt is already closed, return the same successful response the first call returned and write nothing at all, because the fencing guard resolves the current attempt through a helper that ignores closed attempts and would otherwise refuse the second call as superseded — that would break the byte-identical repeat the acceptance case requires. Only then call `assertAttemptCurrent` with the caller's attempt id and generation so a superseded caller is refused with its existing name. Then refuse an attempt that is not in the finalizing phase, since closing a running attempt would hand the seat back without the bytes being landed. Finally move it to closed through the store's phase setter, which is the single write, and return the attempt id, generation, phase and the reported outcome. Record the reported outcome and landed revision in the response and, if the existing activity vocabulary already has a suitable event, the activity log — but do NOT add fields to the attempt schema for them: a durable landing record is the receipt slice's job, and persisting anything extra here would make the repeat call write different bytes. Then register it in `getTools()` in src/tools/index.ts, which a task rail makes mandatory because an unregistered tool is silently invisible to MCP.

NEW src/tools/finalizeAttempt.ts (220 lines). Factory `finalizeAttemptTool(state)` returning a ToolDefinition named exactly `moe.finalize_attempt`. `blocking` is NOT set (task rail) — the whole body runs inside state.runExclusive, which is reentrant via AsyncLocalStorage so the MCP dispatch wrap does not deadlock. inputSchema declares taskId, workerId, runnerId, attemptId, generation, outcome (enum) and landedRevision with additionalProperties:false; required is [taskId, attemptId, outcome].

Handler order IS the design, in this exact sequence:
1. validate — outcome must be in the vocabulary, generation a positive safe integer, landedRevision 40 lowercase hex and REQUIRED when outcome is 'landed' (a bare 'HEAD' or branch name is refused: a receipt built on one would name bytes nobody can find again).
2. task lookup -> notFound (TASK_NOT_FOUND).
3. attempt lookup -> ATTEMPT_NOT_FOUND; wrong task -> ATTEMPT_ID_TASK_MISMATCH, reusing attemptStore's existing name rather than inventing a second one for the same condition.
4. ALREADY-CLOSED SHORTCUT, before any fencing: returns the first call's response and writes nothing. A comment at the site spells out why it may not be tidied below the guard — assertAttemptCurrent resolves through currentAttempt(), which ignores closed attempts, so a repeat would be refused ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED and the bug would look correct in review. It is not a fencing bypass: closing an already-closed attempt changes nothing, and every OPEN case still passes through the guard below.
5. assertAttemptCurrent with the caller's {attemptId, generation} -> ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED by its existing name.
6. phase !== 'finalizing' -> ATTEMPT_NOT_FINALIZING. Closing a `running` attempt would hand the seat back with nothing landed; `reconciling` belongs to the recovery slice.
7. setAttemptPhase(closed) — the single write.

Outcome vocabulary: 'landed' | 'nothing-to-commit' | 'rescued' | 'failed', mapped to the four real endings of the wrapper's landing path (MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, MOE_RESCUE_REF, MOE_COMMIT_FAILED).

NOT persisted: outcome and landedRevision are echoed in the response only. No field was added to ExecutionAttempt, and the unit suite asserts the stored record's key set is EXACTLY the nine schema fields. Persisting them would both change the repeat call's bytes and poach the receipt slice's job. No activity row and no event either — attemptStore's header states that is deliberate (both would need edits to the ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES / StateChangeEvent unions, there is no consumer, and the vocabulary has no attempt-close event), and a write on the repeat would break byte-identity.

implementationPlan.description: DOCUMENT THE TOOL. Add a section for `moe.finalize_attempt` to docs/MCP_SERVER.md, placed with the other lifecycle tools and following the existing section format used by its neighbours: a one-line purpose, a parameters block, a returns block, and a notes list. The notes must state the things a caller cannot guess: that the runner, not the CLI's exit, is what declares a task's bytes final, so an interactive seat that stays open can still finalize; that the call is fenced, so a superseded attempt is refused by name; that it is idempotent, so a retry after a lost response is safe and writes nothing; that closing the attempt is what lifts the finalizing hold on both the worker's next claim and qa_approve; and that the refusal both of those raise carries a retryable flag in its context and must not be treated as fatal. Also state the honest boundary: the reported outcome and landed revision are carried in the call and echoed back but are not yet persisted as a durable delivery record, which is the receipt slice's work. Documentation only — no behaviour change in this step.

Documentation only. Zero behaviour change; no source file touched in this step.

NEW SECTION `### moe.finalize_attempt`, placed immediately after `moe.complete_task` and before `moe.get_commit_scope` — the tool that closes the boundary complete_task opens should be read next to it. Format follows its nearest Wave-1 neighbour `moe.record_candidate`: one-line purpose, Parameters block, Returns block, Notes list, plus an Errors list of JSON-RPC code + codeName pairs.

The notes state the things a caller cannot guess:
- the RUNNER declares the bytes final, not the CLI's exit — an interactive TUI seat stays open long after the work lands, and a provider mode without one-shot semantics has no exit to infer from
- closing lifts BOTH holds (the worker's next claim and qa_approve), and neither depends on anything but the presence of a finalizing attempt
- the refusal both holds raise is -32002 / ATTEMPT_FINALIZING with context {attemptId, generation, taskId, workerId, retryable: true} and MUST NOT be treated as fatal — with the honest caveat that MoeError.context is NOT forwarded over the MCP wire (a wire refusal carries only {code, message, data:{tool, codeName}}), so a remote caller keys on codeName or on the message, which names the attempt and says the refusal is retryable
- fenced by assertAttemptCurrent, so a superseded attempt is refused by name and closes nothing
- idempotent: a retry after a lost response returns the same response and writes nothing (byte-identical .moe/attempts/<id>.json), and the already-closed answer is deliberately evaluated BEFORE the fence, with the reason spelled out and the "this is not a fencing bypass" argument stated
- only a `finalizing` attempt may be closed; a `running` one is refused because closing it would hand the seat back with nothing landed
- THE HONEST BOUNDARY, stated plainly: outcome and landedRevision are carried in the call and echoed back but are NOT persisted — nothing added to the ExecutionAttempt schema, no activity event, no broadcast. A durable delivery record is moe.record_delivery_receipt's job in the receipt slice. The daemon never runs git and has verified neither value; it checks the revision's shape only.
- not blocking; no ownership or status gate (the runner finalizes after complete_task, when QA may already own the REVIEW task, so the attempt fence is the guard)
